doc.title: Ingrid Sertso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, August 11, 2014

title: Artist family, Karl Berger, and meeting Don Cherry in Paris
summary: Raised by a painter brother and pianist mother, she sang standards, met Karl, who found Ornette's record; they met Don Cherry at Buttercup's club in Paris and he brought them to the US.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: painting, music. Because my older brother was also — he brought me actually to my first jazz concert and he always painted with music, you know. He had records and it was his biggest inspiration. And then I got my own agent and I wanted to do jazz and I went into the whole standards thing. And then about three years later after I did it alone, I met Karl and then we wanted to just build something up together. He played piano in the band I worked in and then one day he came home and said, “I think I found what we need.” And he brought “This is Our Music,” the record of Ornette Coleman. And hearing this, we immediately went to Paris. Don Cherry was sitting in Buttercup’s club. Buttercup was the wife of Bud Powell. It was shortly before Bud Powell died in Paris. And she had a club and Don Cherry was sitting there. And Karl said, “Oh, isn’t that the trumpet player on the cover of ‘This is Our Music’?” and he went straight over. We introduced ourselves and Karl was in the band. Me partially. Because the clubs didn’t always pay a singer. So I sat in and I worked with Don as much as possible. And he brought us over here and that’s how we met Ornette.
